items.title: UN nuclear watchdog “increasingly concerned” about Iran’s uninspected Isfahan plant
items.why: A confidential report by the International Atomic Energy Agency, seen by news agencies on Friday, says it does not know the location or status of an enrichment plant Iran declared in Isfahan in 2025. It calls this a serious proliferation concern. Iran says inspections cannot resume amid US threats.
items.matters: The agency says it cannot confirm Iran has not diverted nuclear material, including near-weapons-grade uranium.

items.title: Building under construction collapses near Nairobi, Kenya, killing at least six
items.why: Part of an eight-storey building under construction collapsed on Friday morning in Syokimau, on the outskirts of Kenya’s capital, Nairobi. Public broadcaster KBC and Reuters report six dead and five rescued; another outlet reported five dead and one missing. Preliminary reports point to a failure during concreting.
items.matters: It comes three weeks after a collapse in Nairobi’s Eastleigh district, renewing calls for tighter building safety checks.

items.title: Rosalía wins album of the year at the Latin Grammys for Lux
items.why: Spanish singer Rosalía won album of the year for Lux and song of the year for “La Perla” at the 27th Latin Grammy Awards in Las Vegas on Thursday. Milo J took record of the year for “Niño”, and Colombian singer Aria Vega was named best new artist.
items.matters: Daddy Yankee was honoured as the Latin Recording Academy’s person of the year.

items.title: US says it shot down two Iranian drones aimed at Bahrain
items.why: Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said on Friday they destroyed a US early-warning radar in Bahrain, in retaliation for a strike on a telecoms tower in Sirik, southern Iran. US Central Command called the claim false, saying it shot down two Iranian drones and there was no damage or injury.
items.matters: Reuters says it is Iran’s first claimed attack on US forces in a Gulf country since early September.
items.changed: Updated: the US denies the radar was hit and says it downed two drones
Updated: after Moscow and Dublin meetings, the US says Europe will join the talks
items.title: Europe to join next round of Ukraine peace talks, US envoys say
items.why: After meeting Vladimir Putin in Moscow on Thursday, US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner briefed Volodymyr Zelensky near Dublin and said Europe would join the next round of talks. Zelensky confirmed this. The Kremlin says the EU must first name one representative. No date is set.
items.matters: Kushner says the US is also working towards the largest prisoner exchange of the war.

items.title: Haiti’s police retake the national football stadium, held by gangs since 2024
items.why: Haitian police said on Thursday they had taken full control of the Sylvio Cator stadium in the capital, Port-au-Prince, working with a government security task force and Salvadoran troops. Gangs had held it since 2024. El Salvador’s president, Nayib Bukele, says the forces will use it as a base.
items.matters: Haiti’s national team has had to play home qualifiers in Curaçao; about 2,000 Salvadoran soldiers operate outside the UN-backed force.

items.title: El Niño and global warming drove Indonesia’s worst fires in a decade
items.why: World Weather Attribution scientists say El Niño roughly halved rainfall from July to October, while human-caused warming made the season about 1.6°C hotter and fire weather three times more likely. Drained peatland and deforestation added to the risk; nearly 3 million hectares have burned, monitors estimate.
items.matters: Smoke from the fires has reached millions of people in Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore and Timor-Leste.

items.title: Microsoft restores Outlook and Teams gradually after day-long global outage
items.why: An outage that began at about 16:15 UTC on Thursday disrupted Outlook, Teams and Copilot in at least 74 countries. By Friday Microsoft reported improving server stability and a gradual recovery, though some restored servers briefly failed again. It says it saw no sign of a cyber attack.
items.matters: Governments and businesses rely on it; an adviser in Australia estimates the cost to businesses there at billions of dollars.
items.changed: Updated: services are gradually coming back, but recovery is uneven
Updated: Huang has resigned; finance chief Colette Kress is interim chief executive
items.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia chief after affair raises security concerns
items.why: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia’s chief executive and left its board on Thursday after 33 years, following reports of extramarital affairs, one with a woman reportedly suspected by US intelligence of working for China. Beijing denies this. Finance chief Colette Kress is interim chief executive. Shares fell over 10%.
items.matters: Nvidia makes most of the world’s AI chips, so its leadership affects the whole AI industry.

items.title: UN food agency chief says 900,000 people in Sudan lost food aid
items.why: On his first field trip, the World Food Programme’s new head, Luke Lindberg, met displaced families in Kosti, Sudan, and called for an end to the war: “We cannot outfeed the war.” Funding cuts have shrunk WFP’s reach from over 4 million people in August to just over 3 million.
items.matters: WFP says it needs $520 million to feed 5.4 million people in Sudan through April 2027.

items.title: Manchester United and Crystal Palace both sack their managers
items.why: Manchester United sacked Michael Carrick on Thursday with the club 18th in the Premier League after one league win in ten games. Later that day, bottom club Crystal Palace parted with Pierre Sage after five months. Sky Sports reports Mauricio Pochettino has verbally agreed to take the United job.

items.title: Amnesty says South Sudan and UN failed to prevent village massacre
items.why: Amnesty International says South Sudan’s authorities and the UN mission had about two weeks’ warning before armed men attacked Abiemnom, near the Sudan border, on 1 March. Authorities say at least 213 people were killed. The UN mission says it did its best with limited resources.
items.matters: Amnesty is calling for independent inquiries; South Sudan is due to hold elections on 22 December.

items.title: Pakistan debutant Saqib Khan takes seven wickets against Sri Lanka
items.why: Fast bowler Saqib Khan took 7 for 130 on his Test debut as Sri Lanka were bowled out for 446 on day four of the first Test in Rawalpindi, Pakistan. Sri Lanka lost their last six wickets for 42 runs but still lead by 12 on first innings.
items.matters: He is only the fourth Pakistani to take seven wickets in an innings on Test debut.

items.title: Finland says it detected a strike on a Russian warship nearby
items.why: Finland’s military says it detected a strike on a Russian warship in the Gulf of Finland on Wednesday. Ukraine’s security service says its drones hit the small missile ship Naro-Fominsk; Estonia’s defence minister says smoke was seen and the ship returned towards St Petersburg.
items.matters: Yle reports the strike was near Gogland island, about 40 km from Finland and 55 km from Estonia, both NATO members.

items.title: Israeli strike on Gaza’s Nasser Hospital kills a surgeon and five others
items.why: An Israeli air strike hit the surgery department of Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis, southern Gaza, early on Thursday, killing at least six people including a surgeon, Gaza’s health ministry says. Israel’s military says Hamas was using the hospital as a command centre.
items.matters: Palestinian health authorities say more than 1,600 people have been killed in Gaza since the October 2025 ceasefire.

items.title: Democrat Scott Colom unseats Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi
items.why: Scott Colom, a 43-year-old Democratic prosecutor, defeated Republican Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi after more than a week of counting postal and provisional ballots from the 3 November election. AP called the race on Wednesday evening and Hyde-Smith conceded.
items.matters: He will be Mississippi’s first Black senator since 1881; Democrats have flipped at least eight Republican-held Senate seats.

items.title: Record-breaking liner SS United States sunk to make world’s largest reef
items.why: The SS United States, a 302-metre ocean liner that still holds the transatlantic speed record set in 1952, was deliberately flooded and sunk in the Gulf of Mexico off Florida on Wednesday. It will become the world’s largest artificial reef, about 55 metres down.
items.matters: Florida’s Okaloosa County bought the ship, out of service since 1969, hoping the wreck will draw divers.

items.changed: Updated: the death toll has risen to eight
items.title: Building collapse in Brooklyn, New York, kills eight and injures 17
items.why: A three-storey building on Flatbush Avenue in Brooklyn, New York, collapsed into a neighbouring excavation site on Wednesday afternoon. At least eight people died and 17 were hurt, including three firefighters, Mayor Zohran Mamdani said on Thursday. The cause is being investigated.

items.title: Pope Leo XIV arrives in Peru, his adopted home, for six-day visit
items.why: Pope Leo XIV landed near Lima on Wednesday and was welcomed by President Keiko Fujimori, starting the final leg of a 12-day South American tour after Uruguay and Argentina. He will visit Chiclayo, where he was bishop from 2015 to 2023, Cusco and Pucallpa before leaving on Monday.

items.title: Israel’s cabinet orders preparations for possible strike on Iran, media report
items.why: Israel’s security cabinet, chaired by caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, told the military on Wednesday to step up preparations for a possible attack on Iran, Israeli media reported. Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei warned that bases used against Iran, “from West Asia to Europe”, would be targets.
items.matters: Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot, who is trying to form a government, urged Netanyahu to avoid military action without an immediate threat.

items.title: Saudi Arabia says it intercepted Houthi missiles aimed at Riyadh and Mecca
items.why: The Saudi-led coalition said on Wednesday it destroyed three cruise missiles heading for Riyadh and drones aimed at Mecca and southern regions, the second day of interceptions over the capital. The Houthis denied targeting Mecca. Fighting inside Yemen has also intensified.
items.matters: The WHO says more than 320,000 people in Yemen have been displaced by the fighting since August.

items.changed: Updated: Kenya has discharged its last Ebola patient
items.title: Congo’s Ebola cases pass 11,000 as Kenya discharges its last patient
items.why: Ebola has infected 11,042 people and killed at least 5,387 in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, its government says. The Bundibugyo strain has no approved vaccine. Neighbouring Kenya discharged its last patient on Wednesday and could be declared Ebola-free on 23 December, Health Minister Aden Duale said.
items.matters: It is the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record; Kenya had nine cases and two deaths, all linked to one traveller.

items.title: Former Iraqi MP found dead in Beirut; Lebanon investigates killing
items.why: Ahmed al-Alwani, a former Iraqi lawmaker from Anbar and a critic of Iran’s influence in Iraq, was found dead in a flat in Beirut, Lebanon, on Tuesday evening. A judicial source told AFP he was killed; one Lebanese suspect has been arrested and two Syrians are being sought.

items.changed: Updated: Gibran has formally submitted his resignation
items.title: Indonesia’s vice-president Gibran formally resigns over diploma ruling
items.why: Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka handed his resignation to the People’s Consultative Assembly in Jakarta on Thursday, its speaker Ahmad Muzani said, after courts found his school qualification did not meet election rules. The assembly has up to 60 days to choose a replacement.
items.matters: Gibran is the son of former president Joko Widodo; his case has widened a rift between Prabowo and Widodo, ABC reports.
